questions.question: An agent gave a wrong answer after 40 steps. Why isn't the final answer enough to debug it?
options: It doesn't show which model call or tool call went wrong, how long each took, or what each saw
It is, if you read it carefully
questions.explanation: You need the trajectory, every step with its inputs, outputs, timing and errors, and that's what a trace records.

questions.question: What makes a span the child of another span?
options: It was started while the other span was the current span, so its parent_id is that span's id
It ran after the other one finished
questions.explanation: The tracer records whichever span is current (via contextvars) as the parent when a new span starts.

questions.question: A tool raises inside its span. What should the tracer do?
options: Swallow the exception so the agent keeps going
Mark the span as error, record an exception event, close the span, and re-raise
questions.explanation: Tracing observes; it never changes control flow. Whether to recover is the agent loop's decision.

questions.question: Why use attribute names like gen_ai.usage.input_tokens instead of inventing your own?
options: They're OpenTelemetry's GenAI conventions, so traces work in standard tools without renaming
questions.explanation: Shared conventions make your traces portable across Jaeger, Grafana, Langfuse, Phoenix and others.

questions.question: Spans created inside a plain threading.Thread show up as separate root traces. Why?
options: A new thread starts with an empty context; pass it in with contextvars.copy_context().run(fn)
questions.explanation: asyncio tasks copy the context automatically; plain threads do not. Hand the context over explicitly.

questions.question: In the waterfall, input tokens grow from 412 to 688 across four model calls. What does that tell you?
options: Each call resends the growing conversation history, so cost per step rises as the run goes on
questions.explanation: Agent cost grows with history length. Context management (Phase 4) exists to bend that curve.
